div.head: Had 8
div.ab: And to hadbote, gif fulbrice wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam seofoðan stæpe VII pund to bote, mid godcundan scrifte.
⁊ to hádbote, gif fullbrice wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam seofeðan stæpe VII pund to bote, mid godcundre scrifte.
⁊ to hadbote, gif fullbryce wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam seofoþam stæpe VII pund to bote, mid godcundan scrifte.
Et ad emendationem ordinis, septimo gradu infracto, septem libris supra rectam weram cum penitentia emendet (emendetur cum iniuncta p.).
And to hadbote, gif fullbryce wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere æt þam seofoðam stæpe VII pund to bote, mid godcundan scrifte.
Und wenn tödtliche Verletzung eintritt: ausser dem gesetzlichen Wergeld beim siebenten Ordo [d. h. beim Priester] als Klerusbusse 7 Pfund zur Busse, neben geistlicher Poenitenz.
And if fatal injury occurs: besides the lawful wergild, for the seventh grade [that is, a priest] 7 pounds as compensation for orders, with spiritual penance.

And as compensation for one in orders if a full breach of the peace occurs, the perpetrator must make amends for the seventh rank by paying seven pounds as a penalty in addition to the standard wergild and by doing spiritual penance.

And in compensation for [an offence against a man in] orders, if a full breach occurs, one must pay for the seventh degree with seven pounds in addition to the legal wergild, and intercede zealously with ecclesiastical penance.
div.note: H's ‘seofoþam’ stands so.; U: not in Whitelock’s English Historical Documents, which prints only Had 1–2 and 9–11 (with “…” for the rest); the source of this translation is not recorded.
